articles.title: ‘Emotional intimacy’ from AI chatbots would be banned under Australia’s digital duty of care laws
articles.summary:
Labor government under pressure to create social media watchdog as new online safety standards bill passes lower house

The federal government wants to ban AI chatbots which seek to create…

blocks.text: The federal government wants to ban AI chatbots which seek to create “emotional intimacy” after prime minister Anthony Albanese raised the alarm in a heartfelt speech about children treating these agents as their “best friend”.

But Labor is coming under increasing pressure to empower the telecommunications ombudsman to become a watchdog for social media and AI to give Australians an external complaints mechanism and allow the “naming and shaming” of big tech.

The digital duty of care bill passed the House of Representatives on Wednesday and will be debated by the Senate in coming weeks. The government hopes to pass the bill by the end of 2026, but its pathway through the upper house remains unclear. The Greens support the bill, while the Coalition has said it will not vote for it, though Labor still appears keen to win the opposition’s support and remains open to amendments.

The planned framework would apply new online safety standards to social media, games, apps and chatbots. Labor said it would place “an overarching obligation” on tech platforms “to provide a safe online environment for all Australians” and replace a range of existing online codes and standards with a broader duty-of-care requirement to protect users from certain “harmful” content. It would also require social media platforms to offer an “opt-out” feature for its algorithm and suggested content.

The communications minister, Anika Wells, has suggested content that that promotes misogyny, terrorism, suicide, self-harm and eating disorders would be captured by the laws. On Wednesday, the government accepted amendments from crossbencher Kate Chaney which would add certain AI chatbot activity to the list of harms, requiring platforms to ban “material or conduct that simulates emotional intimacy and encourages or fosters a child’s dependence on it in place of human relationships”.

In an emotional address on Tuesday night, where he again implored the Coalition to consider voting for the bill, Albanese said: “the stories we hear about people identifying a chatbot, a non person as their best friend, should be a huge wake up call for every member of this Parliament to be prepared to act.”

blocks.caption: Prime minister Anthony Albanese speaks during question time in the House of Representatives at Parliament House in Canberra on 27 October. Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAP

blocks.text: The opposition voted against the bill in the House, alongside One Nation. Political opponents have accused Labor of an “Orwellian” system of “censorship” and of seeking to influence conversations online – claims Wells strongly denied.
“If they really care, the test is simple here, they should bring an amendment, not a slogan to ‘kill the bill’,” Wells told ABC radio on Wednesday.

Another Chaney amendment accepted by Labor would require the algorithm opt-out features to be “accessible, easy to use” and “prominently available” on platforms,amid concerns that social media giants may offer only small or hard-to-find features.

The bill now moves to the Senate, where the Greens have set up an inquiry to probe the laws due to report back in late November. Senator Sarah Hanson-Young backed a digital duty of care, calling for the government’s legislation to be strengthened The Greens want Australians to have the right to pursue private legal action against platforms and for penalties to be increased.
“Australians also need an external complaints pathway, free from the profit-driven whims of ‘big tech’s’ content moderation,” she said.

Independent MP Sophie Scamps had proposed changes to the bill to expand the remit of the telecommunications industry ombudsman. She said such a watchdog – which does not currently exist for big tech – would allow ordinary social media users to seek remedies to their accounts being hacked or inaccessible, including compensation, and investigate broader issues to name and shame companies behaving badly.
Labor did not accept this amendment in the lower house and Wells declined to voice support for such an idea, but the Greens will push for such a reform in their Senate negotiations.

Cynthia Gebert, the telecommunications industry ombudsman, said her office would be well placed to carry out such a role for big tech. She said such roles were funded by the industries they regulate and that expanding its remit could be financed by big tech.

“There are some real strengths in the DDOC [digital duty of care] because it’s putting the onus on platforms to make things safe … but I think the area that needs to be strengthened is giving people somewhere to go if they can’t get their complaints resolved with the platform,” Gebert told Guardian Australia.
“It risks leaving Australians in the safe place they are now, where they get automated responses or escalation procedures that don’t go anywhere.”
Gebert said the government should make it mandatory for big tech to be part of an ombudsman scheme, saying it would “hold industry to account and drive system improvement”.
“[The telecommunications industry ombudsman] can help with your Telstra account, but we can’t help with your Gmail account. Consumers come to us sometimes and ask, ‘why this, not that?’,” she said.
“We want to help but don’t have the powers to do so now.”

articles.title: Hackers target US FEC system, disrupting campaign finance disclosures days before midterms
articles.summary: The outage prevents organizations from filing the Federal Election Commission's 24-hour and 48-hour spending reports, which show how much political groups and others are spending on specific races

blocks.text: CYBERSECURITY. Silhouettes of laptop users are seen next to a screen projection of binary code are seen in this picture illustration created on March 28, 2018.
Dado Ruvic/Reuters
The outage prevents organizations from filing the Federal Election Commission's 24-hour and 48-hour spending reports, which show how much political groups and others are spending on specific races

items: The US Federal Election Commission's electronic filing system was hacked, disrupting services just a week before the November 3 elections.
The outage prevents organizations from filing mandatory spending reports, impacting transparency in political spending during a record-breaking election cycle.
Despite the disruption, it does not affect voters' ability to cast ballots, and efforts are underway to restore the filing system.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

NEW YORK, USA – The US Federal Election Commission’s website was targeted by a hacker or hackers, according to an email seen by Reuters, disrupting the agency’s electronic filings system a week before the November 3 elections.

The hack comes as so-called super PACs and dark money groups spend record sums in the final days of the races. The elections will determine whether President Donald Trump’s Republicans maintain their majorities in Congress for the next two years.

In a statement, the FEC said, “At this time, the FEC’s electronic filing system is currently offline and our IT staff are actively working to restore service.” The FEC, which tracks the spending of candidates and political committees, said users could still search the website for past reports. A status message posted by the FEC said its filing system had been down since around 10 pm ET on Monday (0200 GMT; 10:00 am Tuesday Philippine time).

Around 8 pm ET on Tuesday (0000 GMT; 8:00 am Wednesday Philippine time), a new status message said the issue “has been identified and a fix is being implemented.” The FEC did not immediately return a message seeking comment and a notice on its website said its filing system remained offline.
The FEC does not play a role in administering US elections and the outage should have no effect on voters’ ability to cast ballots.
The outage does prevent organizations from filing the FEC’s 24-hour and 48-hour spending reports, which show how much political groups and others are spending on specific races.
“I’ve never seen this in 26 years,” said Steven Mele, president and CEO at political finance compliance firm MBA Consulting Group.
The FEC posted the notice to its website after campaign finance officers could not file mandatory reports late on Monday.

“We have a bad actor attempting to breach FEC systems. As a result, we’ve had to temporarily shut down our web facing services,” an FEC electronic filings officer said in the email to several campaign compliance firms that night.
The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and the FBI both referred questions to the FEC.

The midterms are now the most expensive US election in history with roughly $11.21 billion spent on advertising and future reservations so far, according to political ad tracker AdImpact. They have surpassed the previous record set in the 2024 elections when $11.2 billion was spent on all races, including $3.2 billion on the presidential race between Trump and former Vice President Kamala Harris, AdImpact said.

Much of the spending is being driven by super PACs, which can accept unlimited amounts of money from wealthy individuals and corporations and spend as much as they want on campaigns with few restrictions.
The sums being spent in recent weeks are staggering as Democrats gain ground in several Republican strongholds.

Super PACs and dark money groups have spent an average of over $50 million per day over the last week, said Brendan Glavin, research director at nonpartisan campaign watchdog group OpenSecrets. More than $250 million in spending was reported on October 20 alone, he added.
“It’s a big deal,” he said of the outage, which leaves voters in the dark until the filing system is back online.

“These are the key reports that tell us what is happening,” Glavin said. “In the last days of the election this is the only way for us to keep track of where the money’s being spent” and who’s spending it. – Rappler.com

articles.title: PNP opens hotlines for tips on Bato dela Rosa amid P50M reward
articles.summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) has opened hotlines for information on the whereabouts of Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa as authorities offer a P50-million reward for information leading to his…

blocks.text: Published October 28, 2026 1:21pm

The Philippine National Police (PNP) has opened hotlines for information on the whereabouts of Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa as authorities offer a P50-million reward for information leading to his arrest.

“We have already established hotlines that the public can call or text to provide tips or information on the senator’s whereabouts,” PNP spokesperson Police Colonel Allen Rae Co said at a press briefing on Wednesday.
The public may contact the following numbers:
The PNP urged the public to provide credible information through the designated hotlines or by calling 911.
Co assured potential informants that their identities and contact details would remain confidential.
The P50-million reward will be given to an informant whose verified information leads to Dela Rosa’s arrest, subject to validation, the PNP said.
Co warned that those who deliberately make prank calls or provide false information to obstruct the operation could face criminal charges.
The PNP also reiterated its appeal for Dela Rosa to surrender voluntarily before the one-week deadline set by the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) expires on Friday.
Co said the deadline was intended to give the senator an opportunity to surrender peacefully and avoid a potentially dangerous encounter that could result in injuries or loss of life.
The PNP said authorities had received no indication that Dela Rosa intended to surrender, while police tracking teams were already operational.
Dela Rosa is wanted by the International Criminal Court (ICC) in connection with the crimes against humanity case arising from former President Rodrigo Duterte’s war on drugs.
The senator is accused of being a co-perpetrator in the alleged crimes during his tenure as PNP chief under the Duterte administration.
The DILG earlier claimed that Dela Rosa was hiding in Mindanao under the protection of an “armed and powerful group,” but did not identify the group.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: LTO to start revoking drunk drivers' licenses by November 15
articles.summary: The Land Transportation Office (LTO) will start revoking the licenses of drunk drivers beginning November 15, the agency said Wednesday.

blocks.text: Published October 28, 2026 1:08pm
The Land Transportation Office (LTO) will start revoking the licenses of drunk drivers beginning November 15, the agency said Wednesday.

LTO chief Assistant Secretary Markus Lacanilao explained that while the Anti-Drunk and Drugged Driving Act of 2013 remains in effect, going after offenders would require having to go through the court process. The LTO's jurisdiction, Lacanilao said, is with the drivers' license.

"'Yung mga driver na mahuhuli na naka-inom at magpo-positive doon sa tatlong test, pati doon sa breath analyzer, ang mangyayari sa driver's license niyan, mare-revoke," Lacanilao told GMA News in a phone call.
(Drivers caught drinking and would be positive in the three tests, as well as the breath analyzer, will have their licenses revoked.)
The order will take effect on November 15, ahead of the expected traffic grind of the Christmas season.

According to Lacanilao, the revocation could still be appealed. The case will go through the LTO's Intelligence and Investigation Division, while hearings will be conducted before a resolution is reached.
However, more serious incidents could lead to permanent revocation.
"Kung nakabangga sila, nakapatay sila, perpetual revocation," Lacanilao said.
(If they hit someone, kill someone, this will result in perpetual revocation.)
Lacanilao said incidents of drunk driving have been logged over the years, with Cebu having the most cases. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Marquez’s plan as chief justice bet: No more overburdened courts by 2032
articles.summary: 'While a courtroom or a courthouse is a physical representation of justice, the true measure of a court is not its buildings or facilities, but the quality of justice it provides,' Marquez says

items: Associate Justice Jose Midas Marquez promises to eliminate overburdened courts by 2032 if appointed as Chief Justice, emphasizing the importance of quality justice over physical court structures.

Marquez identifies key issues in the judiciary, including court congestion and delays, and plans to implement a Strategic Plan for Judicial Innovations 2.0 focusing on technology, court management, and judicial independence.
He advocates for legislative support to create more courts, clarify budget roles, and strengthen judicial accountability, while also addressing judges' independence and allowances.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Associate Justice Jose Midas Marquez made a big promise when he faced the Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) for his interview as a chief justice candidate.

Marquez, who once served as head of the Supreme Court’s (SC) Office of the Court Administrator, said there will be no more overburdened courts six years from now if he is selected as Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo’s successor.
“By 2032, we should no longer have [an] overburdened court,” said the aspiring chief justice during his public interview on Monday, October 26.

“While a courtroom or a courthouse is a physical representation of justice, the true measure of a court is not its buildings or facilities, but the quality of justice it provides. Citizens do not come to court because of the structure that houses it; they come because they seek protection of their rights, resolution of disputes, and assurance that the rule of law will prevail,” Marquez added.
Marquez is one of the five SC associate justices in the running to become Gesmundo’s successor. The JBC concluded the interviews on Monday and will proceed to deliberations.
Afterwards, the council will submit to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. a short list of nominees. Marcos will then appoint the country’s 28th chief justice.
Marquez is currently the most junior among the candidates and is holding seat no. 12 at the High Court. If chosen, he will serve as chief justice for 10 years, or until 2036.
During the interview, Marquez said the judiciary faces three perennial problems: congestion of court dockets, delay in resolution of cases, and the perception of alleged corruption.

“So to enhance our court processes, court management, pagandahin pa natin ‘yong internet connectivity not only here in NCR (National Capital Region), but especially in far-flung areas para mas papabilis ang takbo ng resolution ng mga desisyon,” the magistrate said.
“Dapat po meron tayong continuous monitoring of the dockets of all courts nationwide, ‘di lang ang congested courts,” he added.

(So to enhance our court processes, court management, let’s improve our internet connectivity not only here in NCR, but especially in far-flung areas to improve the resolution of cases. We should have a continuous monitoring of dockets of all courts nationwide, not only those which are congested.)
Marquez said that if selected, he will launch his Strategic Plan for Judicial Innovations 2.0 (SPJI) that will run from 2028 to 2032.
SPJI is the brainchild of outgoing Chief Justice Gesmundo which contains the innovations for the judiciary, including digitalization. It has been running since 2022 and will conclude in 2027.
The aspiring chief justice said his SPJI 2.0 will focus on the following:

items: Sustain and institutionalize SPJI reforms
Invest in people development and people encounter
Reinforce the Court as both a place and a service
Strengthen the Judiciary’s independence and fiscal autonomy
Harness technology and digital transformation to address judicial inefficiencies
Continuous monitoring of the Rules of Court
Initiatives for the Philippine Judicial Academy, which is the “training school for justices, judges, court personnel, lawyers, and aspirants to judicial posts.”
Initiatives for the JBC
More power to the Judicial Integrity Office (JIO). This is the SC office that handles administrative disciplinary cases and ensures accountability within the judiciary.

More power to Office of the Judiciary Marshals. This office was established under Gesmundo to deal with threats and violence against members of the bench and court personnel that affect not only their lives and safety, but also undermine judicial independence.

blocks.caption: Marquez’s plan as chief justice bet: No more overburdened courts by 2032

blocks.text: When asked to give at least three laws that the Congress may pass to help the judiciary, Marquez said he wants legislation that will will focus on the creation of more courts – both regular and Shari’ah (Islam) courts.

He said that he also wants a law that clearly defines the role of the Department of Budget and Management in the preparation of the budget of government branches and agencies. Marquez added he also wants a law that will strengthen the mandate, powers, and authority of the SC’s JIO.
As to additional courthouses, Marquez said the construction of halls of justice is not only a concern of the judiciary, but also of local government units (LGU).

“Para sa akin po, ‘yong construction ng hall of justice po, kasi kasama po sa trabaho ng LGU, pasensya na po (For me, the construction of hall of justice is part of the LGU’s job, I’m sorry). Because if you want your LGU to be the best LGU, you have to provide all these services,” he explained.

Marquez also said he wants to standardized the allowances of judges. He explained that it’s an independence issue that some of the judges are receiving allowances from LGUs where their courts are located.

“For me, para po talaga mawala na ‘yong usapin ng independence [of our judges] being encroached upon by the LGUs, may siguro dapat pong pag-usapan or pag-isipang mabuti how we can increase the allowances of our judges and give that allowance,” he said.

(For me, to eradicate the issue on our judges’ independence being encroached upon by the LGUs, maybe we can talk or think carefully how we can increase the allowances of our judges and give that allowance.)

During the interview, Marquez was also asked about the SC’s power of judicial review – or the mandate to revisit whether another branch of government erred in following rules and in case it violated the Constitution.

He explained that his years as associate justice were honed by his past experiences inside the High Court. He explained that when resolving cases involving other branches, he always looks at the mandate of that specific branch.

“That’s the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, the judiciary. Maingat na maingat po ako doon (I am really careful about that). I don’t want to overstep the mandate or overreach the mandates of either the executive or the legislative,” the magistrate said.
If he becomes chief justice, Marquez said he will lead, like Gesmundo, with collegiality.

“Kung paano ang naging pamalakad ni Chief Justice Gesmundo, palagay ko po kaya ko rin pong gawin, tularan, o kung kaya pong higitan pa, gagawin po natin (I can emulate the leadership style of Chief Justice Gesmundo, and if I can go beyond it, we will),” he added.

Marquez also revealed during the interview that his age and experience in the bench – being the most junior candidate – were part of the things he considered when he accepted the nomination. The justice said he rose from the ranks – he started out as an intern, court lawyer, spokesperson, and court administrator.
Marquez said he will lead by example if chosen as the next head of the judiciary.

“Para sa akin, I’ve always led by example. So pinapakita ko lang po na inire-respeto natin silang lahat, nagtatrabaho po tayo nang maayos, at nakikinig po tayo sa lahat ng dapat pong pakinggan (For me, I’ve always led by example. So I just show that I respect everyone, I work professionally, and we listen to those who need to be listened to),” Marquez said.
“You just have to do your work…. Do not look for promotion. Just do your work and do it well. There’s no substitute for hard work,” he added. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Gulf states working on multipart peace deal to avert renewal of US-Iran war
articles.summary:
Talks are aimed at reopening strait of Hormuz and lifting sanctions on Iran, and for Houthis to withdraw in Yemen

A multipronged peace deal to reopen the strait of Hormuz within four days of…

blocks.text: A multipronged peace deal to reopen the strait of Hormuz within four days of sanctions being lifted and for the Houthis to withdraw substantial forces inside Yemen are at the heart of Gulf states’ plans to avert what they regard as a disastrous renewal of war between Iran and the US.
The US is aware of the talks’ progress but is holding out for a concession that European powers suggest could involve Iran allowing UN weapons inspectors back into the country.

The British foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, urged the Iranians to agree to readmit the UN weapons inspectors when he met the Iranian foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, in New York but so far Iran has refused, saying it will only hold talks in principle on its nuclear programme.
European diplomats believe allowing weapons inspectors to reenter Iran and visit its bombed nuclear sites is a minimum requirement for a breakthrough with the US president, Donald Trump.

But Iran remains focused solely on the guarantees of sanctions relief it would receive in return for reopening the strait of Hormuz. Dr Ali Bagheri, the deputy secretary of Iran’s national security council, said Iran was willing to reduce its proposal that the strait reopen seven days after economic sanctions are lifted to four days.

In a further sign of flexibility, Iran is starting to acknowledge it has a mediating role in the parallel conflict in Yemen. Iran’s secretary of the supreme national security council, Mohsen Rezaei, met the Houthi’s ambassador to Iran, Ibrahim al-Dulaimi, on Tuesday.

The meeting took place 24 hours after a high-level delegation from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan travelled to Tehran to discuss Saudi terms for ending the Yemen conflict as well as a longer-term security architecture for the region.

Iran backs the Houthis, and has the power to influence them, including devising proposals that stop short of a Houthi military victory that many say is unobtainable. In return the Houthis are demanding that Saudi Arabia lift what it regards as a naval and air blockade on Houthi-held territory.

Iran successfully prevented discussion of its nuclear programme at the meeting with Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, and instead ensured the focus was a broader discussion about a long-term regional security vision that would include the Gulf states and Iran and see the US presence in the Middle East reduced or ended.
A new non-aggression pact in which Iran is no longer ostracised by the rest of the Gulf, as it has been since the 1979 Islamic Revolution, would meet Iran’s highest strategic goal.

An agreed commitment to this goal by six Gulf states might also make it easier for Iran to swallow potentially difficult tactical concessions that it would be required to make concerning its nuclear programme.
One of the key advocates of the inclusive security plan, Oman’s foreign minister, Badr Albusaidi, said he believed the US administration understood this was the direction the region is heading.

He said: “I think if Iran is fully re-engaged in this idea of having all of us, eight countries at peace with the rest of the world, the economic potential is going to be enormous for all of us in the region and those outside the region who choose to take part in this development. We have really discussed this in at length during the talks between Iran and the United States, and I think there is general acceptance that this will be the direction of travel once we have a deal in place at the end of the day.”

At a televised event in Iran this week Araghchi underlined the importance of a new postwar security pact to Iran, saying: “Recently, there has been talk of a new war but I am already thinking about the postwar period. Whether there is war or not, our policies remain the same.”

articles.title: Gulliver fans celebrate three centuries of Jonathan Swift’s classic satire
articles.summary:
Events in Ireland explore origins of Gulliver’s Travels, the Dublin clergyman’s book that became an instant hit in 1726

In March 1726, an Irish clergyman visited London and arranged for a…

blocks.text: In March 1726, an Irish clergyman visited London and arranged for a courier to deliver a manuscript to a publisher under cover of night. The dean of St Patrick’s Cathedral in Dublin knew his novel would cause trouble and wanted to publish it anonymously.

His name was Jonathan Swift and the story was called Travels into Several Remote Nations of the World. The satirical work was published that October and is better known 300 years on as Gulliver’s Travels.

An immediate sensation, it skewered Georgian pretensions and entered popular culture through translations, children’s versions, comics and films. The anniversary is now being celebrated at Swift’s alma mater, Trinity College Dublin, and at events around Ireland.

blocks.caption: The Lilliputian army marches beneath Gulliver in Florence Dugdale’s Gulliver’s Travels Told in Simple Language (1912). Illustration: Digital Collections Department/Trinity College Dublin

blocks.text: Exhibitions, festivals, seminars, art competitions and workshops are exploring the origins of Swift’s masterpiece, its retelling through a feminist lens, and its prophetic depiction of a society in thrall to a form of artificial intelligence.

“Lemuel Gulliver’s first voyage to the land of Lilliput is the one most familiar to audiences today,” said Stephanie Breen, an assistant librarian and co-curator of the exhibition at Trinity. “This exhibition, however, brings viewers on a journey to all of the lands Gulliver encountered – Lilliput, Brobdingnag, Laputa and beyond and the country of Houyhnhnms.”

blocks.caption: A 1726 edition of Jonathan Swift’s novel, initially known as Travels into Several Remote Nations of the World. Photograph: Digital Collections Department/Trinity College Dublin

blocks.text: The exhibition, which runs until December and is available online, draws on the university’s collection of hundreds of editions and popularisations of Gulliver’s Travels, including engraved illustrations, pop-up versions, a 1976 Marvel comic and the only known surviving copy of an abridgement printed in 1761.

The voice of Gulliver’s wife, Mary, who is neglected and left at home “big with child” until his eventual, grumpy return, was imagined through contemporary works such as Alison Fell’s The Mistress of Lilliput and Lauren Chater’s Gulliver’s Wife, said Aileen Douglas, a professor of English and exhibition co-curator.

Gulliver’s experiences in Laputa, a floating island dedicated to arts and science, resonated with our era’s anxieties about technology, said Douglas. Its inhabitants seek to extract sunbeams from cucumbers and obtain knowledge via an “engine” of wires, handles and paper that can produce tracts on philosophy, poetry and mathematics “without the least assistance from genius or study”.
In the kingdom of Luggnagg, Gulliver is at first enchanted and then horrified by the Struldbruggs, a race that is immortal but continues eternally to age and sicken.

A panel discussion about the role of art in challenging power, and Gulliver’s attacks on human vanity and scientific arrogance, is to be held at Trinity on Wednesday. At the cathedral, a children’s choir will perform the premiere of a work by the composer Seán Doherty, along with organ recitals and extracts of Gulliver’s Travels read by the Swift scholar Brendan Twomey. An exhibition and lecture series at the Robinson library in County Armagh runs until December.

Born in 1667, Swift combined posts in the Church of Ireland with pamphlets and essays that pioneered deadpan, savage satire, including A Modest Proposal, which suggested alleviating the plight of the Irish poor by selling their children as food to the wealthy.
after newsletter promotion
He wrote Gulliver’s Travels in Dublin and at an estate in County Meath, where it is said that some very tall and very small farm workers inspired the storytelling.

When shipwrecked on Lilliput, Gulliver discovers diminutive inhabitants who are waging war against a rival kingdom in a dispute over which end of a boiled egg should be cracked – a satire on Europe’s sectarian conflicts. Gulliver captures the Blefuscudian fleet and douses a fire at a Lilliputian palace by urinating on it.

blocks.caption: Gulliver puts out a palace fire in Lilliput by urinating on it in Gulliver, a retelling by Mary Webb, illustrated by Lauren O’Neill. Photograph: The O’Brien Press

blocks.text: Marooned among giants in Brobdingnag, Gulliver’s stories about his “own dear native country” inadvertently reveal its corruption and cruelty, prompting the Brobdingnagian ruler to pillory humanity as “the most pernicious race of little odious vermin that nature ever suffered to crawl upon the surface of the earth”.
Swift’s publisher, Benjamin Motte, did not know his author’s identity but the book’s success, and Swift’s literary record, enabled many to guess, said Douglas. “People sort of knew it was him.”

articles.title: After journalist's arrest, lawyers ask whether PNP still 'used' by Duterte family
articles.summary: Missteps by the police who carried out the arrest of veteran journalist Philip Lustre Jr. over the weekend contributed to the denial of his due process, his lawyers said.

blocks.text: October 28, 2026 | 12:43pm

Veteran journalist Philip Lustre Jr. is escorted by police officers at the Quezon City Police District Kamuning Station 10 in Quezon City on Oct. 24, 2026, following his arrest over a cyber libel case filed in Davao City.
The STAR / Miguel de Guzman
MANILA, Philippines — Missteps by the police who carried out the arrest of veteran journalist Philip Lustre Jr. over the weekend contributed to the denial of his due process, his lawyers said.

Besides the alleged procedural lapses by the Davao City Prosecutor’s Office — whose chief prosecutor faces conflict-of-interest questions over his ties with the Duterte family — Lustre’s lawyers also scored the cops for how they served the warrant to the 72-year-old journalist.

Cops from the Quezon City Police District arrested Lustre on Saturday, October 24, at the end of the weekly Saturday News Forum. De Leon was there as a guest speaker and stepped in as Lustre's counsel on the spot.
The warrant, issued October 2 by Judge Retrina Fuentes of the Davao City Regional Trial Court Branch 10, charges Lustre with online libel under the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.

Dino De Leon and other lawyers of the DARGON law firm said at a briefing Wednesday, October 28, that while they recognize the duty of police to serve court-issued warrants, Lustre’s was carried out in a manner that prevented him from being aware of the charges in the first place.

Because the Davao court was closed on Saturday, De Leon recalled his team's struggle to obtain the certified copies of the charge sheet and the prosecutor’s resolution needed for bail. Four lawyers worked on it at the same time to secure Lustre’s release, he said.
“A person’s access to bail should not depend on whether his lawyers can overcome a weekend obstacle course,” De Leon said.
De Leon also questioned why the 72-year-old had to be handcuffed. A request to loosen Lustre’s handcuffs while he was at the hospital was turned down, he added.
“Did he attempt to escape? Did he threaten anyone?” he said, adding that police should identify the specific circumstances that justified the restraint.

The arresting officers also could not inform Lustre who had filed the complaint or what it alleged, according to his legal team. The lawyers learned those details two days later, after they flew to Davao to obtain the documents.

“What’s more difficult and painful than seeing a 72-year-old journalist in handcuffs is seeing a 72-year-old journalist in handcuffs who does not even know the allegations against him,” lawyer Mark David Dacula said.
The complaint, filed by Manases Carpio, the husband of Vice President Sara Duterte, stems from a March 6 Facebook post by Lustre, according to the charge sheet.
This Facebook post had supposedly linked Carpio to an alleged P300-million payment to the 18 self-claimed former bagmen. Lustre’s lawyers, however, said the post merely asked a question.
The lawyers raised the possibility of a double standard in Lustre’s arrest, especially when contrasted with the handling of the vice president’s own case more than a month ago.

A Quezon City court had ordered Duterte’s arrest on September 4 on three counts of grave threats against the president and his family. She appeared in court the next day and posted bail without being handcuffed.
The lawyers also cited Sen. Bato dela Rosa, who remains at large despite an International Criminal Court (ICC) warrant made public in May, and businessman Atong Ang, also a fugitive.
The government last week offered a P50-million bounty for Dela Rosa’s capture.
"Those are the questions we have for Philippine National Police... They should not be instruments of any powerful individual, especially in the administration of justice," Dacula said.

Pointing out that the ICC itself has flagged the "weaponization" of the police under Duterte, De Leon asked the PNP as an institution to consider how far it would "allow itself to be used" against the public.

“I hope and I pray that the institution of the Philippine National Police will reflect until what extent they will be perceived, or actually be used by the Duterte family," he said. "It’s a painful question, but I think it has to be asked."

articles.title: Tampa Bay Rays stun Milwaukee Brewers with late Game 4 win, keeping World Series hopes alive
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays have kept their World Series dreams alive by eking out a late-game, 4-3 win in extra innings over the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4.

image.caption: Tampa Bay Rays outfielder Chandler Simpson reacts after hitting a single in the bottom of the 12th inning of Game 4 of the World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers. (Nathan Ray Seebeck/Imagn Images/Reuters)

blocks.text: MLB·Updated
The Tampa Bay Rays have kept their World Series dreams alive by eking out a late-game, 4-3 win in extra innings over the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4.
Rays come back in bottom of 12th inning to claim 4-3 victory in Game 4

Jonny DeLuca and pinch-hitter Ben Williamson singled home runs in a stunning 12th-inning rally, and the Tampa Bay Rays staved off World Series elimination with a 4-3 win over the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday night that forced Game 5.
Cooper Pratt hit a tiebreaking home run off Ian Seymour in the top of the 12th as Milwaukee neared a sweep and its first World Series title.

But the Rays, also seeking their first championship, rallied in the bottom half after a throwing error by third baseman Joey Ortiz on Junior Caminero's leadoff grounder against reliever Antonio Senzatela.
Liam Hicks singled off Shane Drohan, who relieved in his first appearance since Oct. 15, and DeLuca's single to centre drove in pinch-runner Cedric Mullins to tie the score at 3.
Chandler Simpson's single loaded the bases and Milwaukee employed a five-man infield with the infield in.

Cooper Pratt (right) is seen celebrating a solo home run he hit in the top of the 12th inning of Game 4. The Brewers went up 3-2, but ended up losing the game in the bottom-half of the inning. (Kim Klement Neitzel/Imagn Images/Reuters)
Williamson, who had been 1 for 15 in the postseason, hit a chopper over first baseman Jake Bauers and into right field.
Game 5 will be Wednesday night at Tropicana Field.
Tampa Bay became just the fifth of 26 teams that fell behind 3-0 in the World Series to win Game 4. The previous four lost Game 5.

Of 43 teams to trail 3-0 in any best-of-seven postseason matchup, the only one that rebounded to win was the Boston Red Sox against the New York Yankees in the 2004 American League Championship Series.

articles.title: Luistro: P1.31-B infra budget for my district was proposed by DPWH
articles.summary: Batangas second district representative and House justice committee chair Gerville Luistro on Wednesday said the P1.31 billion worth of infrastructure projects allocated for her district under the…

blocks.text: Published October 28, 2026 12:32pm

Batangas second district representative and House justice committee chair Gerville Luistro on Wednesday said the P1.31 billion worth of infrastructure projects allocated for her district under the House-approved 2027 national budget is around the same amount proposed by the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH).
This was Luistro's was response to criticisms made by budget watchdog People’s Budget Coalition (PBC) which identifies the budget amendments made by the House as “insertions.”
PBC tagged Luistro for having one of the largest DPWH allocation for her district with P1.31 billion.

Luistro, however, said that requests for funding of infrastructure projects are first submitted by the DPWH district engineering offices, then to the Regional Office, and finally to the Central Office.

She added that the DPWH Central Office’s budget proposal will then be subjected to the approval of the Department of Budget and Management (DBM), since it is the DBM which submits the proposed national budget of the President or the National Expenditure Program (NEP) to the House of Representatives and the Senate.

“The process is very tedious. When the NEP reaches the House, it is deliberated by the Appropriations Committee then before the House plenary, when amendments are made for the approval of the House General Appropriations Bill. I don’t understand how things like that [of me being tagged as having one of the highest allocations] will happen,” Luistro said in an interview on Super Radyo dzBB.

“What was reported to me was what was included in the NEP [for the Second District of Batangas] was included as well in the House General Appropriations Bill [we approved on third reading]. I was told it was almost the same amount,” Luistro added.
Cong. Gerville Reyes-Luistro, aminadong walang alam sa sinasabing budget insertion https://t.co/xzvK7i1TR8— DZBB Super Radyo (@dzbb) October 28, 2026
Basis
Luistro also said she made inquiries on the DPWH district engineering office involved, and that the same DPWH district engineering office could not figure out where the P1.3 billion came from.
“I asked the district office about the P1.3 billion, and they could not find the basis of that amount,” Luistro added.
Nevertheless, Luistro said she is still finding out how such budget amendment or “insertion” is being attributed to her.
“I would like to express my interest to see that list so I can verify for myself also what really happened,” Luistro said.
But as far as PBC's Nadine Suzara is concerned, the 2027 budget approved by the House is a "very politician-centered budget."
"It does not address our long term problems: Lack of healthcare, education, malnutrition, stunting, lack of livelihood assitance, among others," Suzara said in a separate dzBB interview.

"Of the P7.2 trillion, we will only have P1.515 trillion because the rest will go to debt service, shares of local government in the tax collection, the cost of running the government such as salaries of workers and maintenance and other operating expenses," Suzara added. —Llanesca Panti/ VAL, GMA News

blocks.text: Live

Cyclone Arnab is making a slow-motion landfall at India's east coast with states evacuating thousands of residents. Also, a new report says India is among nations with highest heatwave exposure for infants. Follow live

blocks.text: What you need to know

items: Cyclone Arnab makes prolonged landfall along coast of Andhra Pradesh
New study says India among top countries with highest heatwave exposure for infants and elderly

blocks.text: Here's a roundup of the biggest news from India on Wednesday, October 28:
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add us as a Preferred Source on Google. Then tap the "Star" or "Preferred" to keep DW News at the top of your feed.
October 28, 2026
Cyclone Arnab batters Andhra Pradesh with drawn-out landfall
"Very severe" Cyclone Arnab made a sooner-than-expected landfall along India's east coast and is now "practically stationary" at the edge, authorities said.
The storm, with winds over 125 kilometers per hour (78 miles per hour) and gusts of 150 kilometers per hour (93 miles per hour), is in the third-highest category of storms on a scale of five.

The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) said its landfall would last for over two hours and that the edge of the storm was already on the coast of the south-eastern state of Andhra Pradesh. Its center remains over sea.

blocks.caption: This is a satellite view of Cyclone Arnab making landfall on the east coast of IndiaImage: CSU/CIRA & EUMETSAT/REUTERS

blocks.text: Power, transport disrupted

The cyclone brought heavy rains, high winds and disruption to Andhra and its neighboring state of Odisha. Gales rocked trees, winds and heavy rain disrupted power lines and the storm caused the sea to surge like many locals had never seen before. Flight and train services were also impacted.
"There was a cyclone here three years ago, but the water didn't rise this much," a 35-year-old local resident said, adding that the government had warned them to stock up on groceries beforehand.
The weather agency warned of "total destruction" of thatched houses, localized flooding, the uprooting of power and communications poles, and "widespread damage" to standing crops.
No casualties so far
No loss of life has been reported in either states as of Wednesday morning.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu credited advance precautionary measures for preventing casualties so far. He said so during a teleconference meeting to monitor the impact of the storm onground, news agency Press Trust of India reported.
Together, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha evacuated nearly 100,000 people from vulnerable regions in preperation of the storm. They were moved inland fro better shelter.

blocks.caption: Thousands of people from coastal, low-lying regions have been moved inlandImage: Noah Seelam/AFP

blocks.text: "Our homes get flooded, and we have to stay in the water," said Rajeshwari, 65, who gave only one name and had been taken to a government-run shelter near Kakinada. "So the government provided us with a bus, and we came here to shelter," she told AFP.

In Nepal, authorities warned tourists against ​venturing into high-altitude areas ‌due to fears that Arnab could trigger torrential downpours, snowstorms and avalanches in the Himalayan region from Thursday night ​through Saturday.

Arnab formed on Monday morning in the Bay of Bengal, a region known for birthing some of the deadliest storms to batter India. This year's season, however, is turbocharged by the El Nino weather phenomenon which is causing unprecedented warming, experts say.

articles.title: Pasig cop apologizes for gun-pointing incident as NAPOLCOM probes case
articles.summary: A police officer in Pasig City on Wednesday apologized after a viral video showed him allegedly pointing a gun at people while intoxicated.

blocks.text: Published October 28, 2026 12:27pm
A police officer in Pasig City on Wednesday apologized after a viral video showed him allegedly pointing a gun at people while intoxicated.
At a press conference, the National Police Commission (NAPOLCOM) presented the cop identified as Police Staff Sergeant Ryan Rene Balisi.

"Sa aking complainant, humihingi po ako ng tawad. Pasensya na po sa aking maling nagawa. Sana mapatawad mo ako. Sa aking mga kababayan sa buong Pilipinas, sana po ma-ano niyo po ako sa aking mga ginawa ay talaga namang pong inaamin ko pong mali," Balisi said.

(To my complainant, I apologize. I am sorry for what I did wrong. I hope you can forgive me. To my countrymen across the Philippines, I hope you can forgive me for what I did, I truly admit that I was wrong.)
"At sa ating kapulisan, Sir, Ma'am, ako po ay humihingi ng tawad dahil sa mga ginawa ko. Sa mga ibang kapulisan po, huwag niyo po akong tularan na ginawa ko po ito," he added.
(And to our police force, Sir, Ma'am, I apologize for what I did. To other policemen, please don't follow what I did.)
Balisi said he had an argument with his wife before the incident, then decided to follow her when she left their home. He admitted that he lost control of his emotions.
Pasig City Police officer-in-charge Police Colonel Wilson delos Santos said authorities acted promptly after receiving the video and identifying Balisi as the police officer involved.
Police tracked Balisi to his residence and brought him to the station. His firearm was confiscated, and an alcohol breath test was administered.
Balisi had posted bail but remained under restrictive custody upon the order of the regional director. He was also set to be reassigned to the Eastern Police District headquarters.
NAPOLCOM Commissioner Ralph Calinisan said his office would proceed with the administrative complaint filed by the complainant against Balisi.
"May complainant dito sa insidenteng ito laban kay Balisi. So that's why itong complainant na ito, ang siyang naghabla kay Balisi dito sa NAPOLCOM," Calinisan said.
(There is a complainant here in this incident against Balisi. So that's why this complainant is the one who filed the complaint against Balisi here at NAPOLCOM.)
"And we will proceed in handling this complaint. 'Yung complaint most likely will progress to two cases, grave misconduct at saka conduct unbecoming of a police officer," he added.
(And we will proceed in handling this complaint. The complaint most likely will progress to two cases, grave misconduct and conduct unbecoming of a police officer.)
Calinisan pointed out that personal problems and intoxication are not excuses for threatening people with a firearm, adding that such incidents undermine public trust in the police.
Meanwhile, Calinisan said the NAPOLCOM would continue strengthening the screening of police applicants, including comprehensive background investigations and proper neuropsychiatric evaluations.
He also emphasized the need to address the mental health and welfare of serving police officers, noting that the commission had reached out to psychologists and psychometricians for assistance.
Calinisan said police officers experiencing personal difficulties should seek professional help, but reiterated that mental health concerns do not excuse abusive behavior. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Israel election results live: exit polls point to tie between Netanyahu and Eisenkot blocs
articles.summary: Both blocs would fall short of the 61 seats needed to form a government as support for Palestinian parties surges

blocks.text: Summary
It’s just after 6am in Tel Aviv where Israelis are waking up to exit polls that show no clear victor in yesterday’s elections, with uncertainty guaranteed at this point.

The polls published by Israel’s major TV networks show Benjamin Netanyahu’s governing bloc tied with the opposition grouping led by Gadi Eisenkot on 51 seats each, short of the 61 seats needed to form a majority coalition government.

Earlier exit polls had Eisenkot winning most seats in the Knesset by a slight margin. Israeli exit polls are often revised after publication and are notoriously imprecise, with the final count often swinging by several seats.

Voter turnout surged to the highest level in more than two decades, underscoring the stakes of an election that has been labelled the most important in the country’s history. More than 77% of eligible voters cast a ballot, according to Israel’s central elections committee, about 7 percentage points higher than in 2022.
Final counting is ongoing, with more than 30% of the votes tabulated so far.

blocks.caption: A supporter of the Likud party waits at an election night rally in Jerusalem. Photograph: Jewel Samad/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: The Palestinian parties are projected to dramatically increase their representation in the Knesset, with predictions they could win as many as 18 seats, up from 10. Experts have said that if Eisenkot falls short of a majority, as the exit polls suggest, he would be obliged to sit down to talk to the Palestinian groupings, the Joint List and Ra’am, to try to form a government – which could take weeks.
It is also possible that Eisenkot could try to govern as a minority government, with informal vote-by-vote agreements that would keep the new coalition afloat.

items: Netanyahu took the stage at a post-election rally in Jerusalem just after 3am, telling his supporters official results will show that “Likud is the largest party in Israel”. He told his supporters that the country must “establish a strong, right-wing national government” – adding that a government that relies on the support of Palestinian parties must not be formed.

Eisenkot told cheering supporters in Tel Aviv that the “Israeli public has voted against Netanyahu’s service as Israel’s prime minister … a worthy leader would have accepted the people’s non-confidence and announced today his retirement from politics.” In his speech, he also warned Netanyahu not to “use Israel’s security” for political ends, playing on fears that the prime minister could use this period of uncertainty to launch a new attack on Iran.

The exit polls were released after a last-ditch effort by Netanyahu and several other parties to keep polling stations open beyond their 10pm deadline was rejected by the Central Elections Committee. The prime minister suggested publicly that efforts were being made by the “left and Arabs” to steal the election, a claim rejected by the committee, which said it had seen no evidence of systematic tampering.

blocks.text: Key events

items: 22m agoSummary

blocks.text: Supporters of the opposition bloc breathed a sigh of relief after the first exit polls were announced, but as the night has worn on nervousness has grown on both sides.

With exit polls shifting to put the two sides on equal footing, Agence France-Presse is reporting that voters like former Hamas hostage Ohad Ben Ami have expressed alarm that Netanyahu could come out ahead.

blocks.caption: Ohad Ben Ami speaks at a Yashar party election night rally. Photograph: Noam Galai/Getty Images

blocks.text: “Three years ago, the government abandoned us,” he said.
double quotation markAn Israeli citizen should never have spent a year and a half in Hamas tunnels when deals [with Hamas] were on the table.”
Netanyahu kept supporters waiting until past 3am in a Jerusalem convention centre. Known for his long, passionate speeches, he was unusually brief.

blocks.caption: Benjamin Netanyahu speaks at his party headquarters. Photograph: Ronen Zvulun/Reuters

blocks.text: Ari Marx, holding a large sign bearing the prime minister’s image, said he was not “scared” of the results or of another war with Iran, which Netanyahu has threatened.
“Either Bibi is going to win or there’s going to be a new election,” he said, using Netanyahu’s nickname, doubting anyone else could form a government.

President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Wednesday allayed concerns as the Philippine peso hit a new historic low, breaching the P64:$1 level.
“Well, first of all, do not take it with alarm. Don't panic,” Marcos said in an ambush interview at the Bureau of Corrections in Muntinlupa City.
The President said that his government is trying to defend the peso “as hard as we possibly can.”

“People can take solace in the fact that our policy towards the peso is to continue to defend the peso as hard as we possibly can. We have all the tools to defend the peso. We have all the means to defend the peso,” Marcos said.

“And with that in mind, we will continue to do all that we can to make sure that the value of the peso does not continue to go down, especially relative to the dollar. The dollar is also becoming very strong. But nevertheless, we have the means, as I say,” he added.
The local currency sank to an intraday low of P64.18:$1, weaker than the 33rd record low of P64.17:$1 seen during Tuesday’s closing.
The local unit’s weakness came amid the continuous spike in global crude oil prices due to the Middle East crisis. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: ‘Backdrop for countless local love stories’: Geelong gingko named Victorian tree of the year
articles.summary:
National trust of Victoria award celebrates much-loved arboreal icons while calling for protection of green spaces

For more than 160 years, a humble ginkgo tree raised from seed in Geelong’s…

blocks.text: For more than 160 years, a humble ginkgo tree raised from seed in Geelong’s botanic gardens has been the backdrop to “countless local love stories”. Standing beneath it is the most popular spot to get married at the park, its branches forming the backdrop of many wedding photos.

Now, in addition to being the largest ginkgo biloba in the state – and possibly Australia – at a whopping 20 metres tall, it has a new claim to fame. The much-adored Geelong icon has been crowned Victoria’s tree of the year.

The National Trust of Australia (Victoria), which runs the awards, announced on Tuesday that Geelong’s ginkgo beat eight other finalists to the 2026 title, receiving 27% of 4,435 public votes cast. Second place went to the smooth bark apple myrtle in Prahran, while Apollo Bay’s myrtle beech was voted third.

To be eligible, trees have to be listed on the National Trust significant tree register, which recognises 2,500 trees in Victoria for their cultural, scientific, and historic value. More than 40 were nominated this year, then narrowed down to nine by a panel of 12 experts and arboriculturists.
The executive manager of gardens and landscapes at the National Trust Victoria, Justin Buckley, said the ginkgo was a “very popular winner”.

blocks.caption: The tree has distinctive stalactite-like growths from its trunk and branches, a feature that only appears on older female gingkos.  Photograph: Daniel Cornell/National Trust Victoria

blocks.text: “It’s a really special tree, and very well loved in that area,” he said.

The ginkgo was planted in 1859, just two decades after the township of Geelong was formally established. The seeds were transported from China, rumoured to have been delivered by a ship’s captain making a stop at Geelong’s port.

Since then, generations of botanic garden workers and volunteers have helped it thrive. Not all have been able to see the unusual stalactite-like growths from its trunk and branches, which only occur in much older female gingko varieties, or enjoy its fruit – which has a reputation for being smelly.

Ginkgos, also known as maidenhairs, are among the most ancient trees on earth, dating back to the Jurassic period more than 160m years ago. In Japan, they’re a symbol of hope, longevity and peace, after six survived the 1945 atomic blast in Hiroshima. They were thought to be extinct in the wild for many centuries before being revived.
Botanic gardens supervisor Sheree Parker said the ginkgo was one of the first trees planted in the park and was also its “most visited and talked about”.
“It’s just starting to awaken now after being dormant,” she said. “We’re really excited.
“It’s our most popular destination to get married as well. We have a lot of weddings on this lawn and a lot of couples like to get married underneath the ginkgo.”
The city of greater Geelong staff had been strongly lobbying for the ginkgo to be crowned since the finalists were announced, posting regularly to social media encouraging people to vote.
“As … the backdrop for countless local love stories, she holds a special place in all our hearts,” they said a post earlier this month.
The competition was established in 2016 to celebrate Victoria’s best-loved trees, while also calling for greater protection of green spaces.

A recent urban greening framework, released by Stonnington city council, found over the past decade, more than 17.9 hectares of tree canopy had been lost on private lands in the inner Melbourne suburb alone.

The National Trust is urging the Victorian government to give automatic statutory protection to trees on its register and those of local councils, while also introducing a “retain first” planning principle making tree removal a genuine last resort.

In the past year, the Victorian government introduced uniform protection of canopy trees, but Buckley said it remained “quite limited” and there was “large scope” for significant trees to be removed without a permit.

“The reason we continue to draw attention to trees through this competition is because they really don’t have adequate protection, certainly not the same protection that heritage buildings have,” Buckley said.
“You can’t just think, well, we’ll take this one out, we’ll put another tree in there and everything will be fine. Big significant trees are virtually irreplaceable.
“As we need to accommodate growing populations and more housing … there’s going to be a lot of pressure on trees.”

articles.title: Ex-Sara Duterte aide Jefry Tupas accuses NBI of harassment over recommendation of charges
articles.summary: Former Davao City chief information officer Jefry Tupas on Wednesday accused the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) of harassment.

blocks.text: Published October 28, 2026 10:40am
Former Davao City chief information officer Jefry Tupas on Wednesday accused the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) of harassment.
This was after the bureau recommended the filing of charges against Tupas before the Department of Justice (DOJ).
“I denounce the NBI’s recommendation to file charges against me before the Department of Justice (DOJ). This is harassment, plain and simple,” he said.
“The NBI can file all the trumped-up charges they want against me, but I will never allow myself to be used as a witness for a case built on lies,” he added.
GMA News Online has reached out to the NBI for comment, but it has yet to reply as of posting time.
The NBI earlier filed a referral with the DOJ against Tupas for cyberlibel, obstruction of justice, and publication of false news.
This stemmed from the sworn statement submitted by dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr.

Gracioso claimed that he delivered cash to Vice President Sara Duterte, former President Rodrigo Duterte, and Davao Representative Paolo Duterte on the instructions of former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
He also claimed that Tupas received the cash on behalf of the Vice President.
Tupas has denied Gracioso’s claims and submitted his affidavit with the bureau.
Sara Duterte, Paolo Duterte, and Velasco have submitted affidavits denying the allegations against them.
'Deceptive maneuvers'
Tupas, meanwhile, alleged that NBI agents offered him cash and a place to stay in the upscale Forbes Park in Makati City.

In his new statement, Tupas questioned the NBI investigation saying he had presented evidence to disprove allegations made by Gracioso including airline ticket bookings, passport photos bearing stamps, and Facebook posts.

Tupas disputed NBI chief Melvin Matibag's statement that he was the source of information about threats to his security. According to Tupas, NBI agents, led by Special Assistant for Mindanao Concerns Voltaire Rovira, were the ones who went to his home in North Cotabato on the morning of September 29.
He noted that he did not ask the NBI to issue a subpoena.
According to him, he requested a formal invitation from Matibag during a telephone conversation regarding the NBI's offer to place him under protective custody.
“Imbes na invitation letter, ang ibinigay ng NBI noong hapon ng September 29, 2026 ay isang subpoena na may petsang September 28, 2026—isang araw bago pa man sila dumating sa aming bahay,” he said.
(Instead of an invitation letter, what the NBI gave on the afternoon of September 29, 2026 was a subpoena dated September 28, 2026—a day before they even arrived at our house.)
He questioned the agency's motives.

“Now that he has publicly identified me as a witness, the apprehension over Matibag’s invitation for a meeting in Manila and the offer for a protective custody becomes completely justified,” Tupas said.
“It is now glaringly obvious that these were not genuine gestures for my safety, but rather deceptive maneuvers to trap me and force me into becoming a false witness,” he added.
Tupas alleged that he was being harassed and pressured to testify against the Vice President in a plunder case linked to Gracioso's allegations.

“It is clear to me, and probably to everyone else who can read between the lines, that I am being harassed, intimidated, and pressured to turn against Vice President Sara Duterte and testify against her in a plunder case related to the Gracioso allegations (as shown in the September 28, 2026 subpoena delivered to my house),” he said. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: US costs of Iran war rise to over $47B – Pentagon data
articles.summary: The Pentagon's latest estimate is tied to the operational costs of carrying out the war, with a projected cost of more than $29 billion to replace expended munitions used in the conflict

blocks.text: PENTAGON. The Pentagon building is seen in Arlington, Virginia, US, October 9, 2020.
Carlos Barria/REUTERS
The Pentagon's latest estimate is tied to the operational costs of carrying out the war, with a projected cost of more than $29 billion to replace expended munitions used in the conflict

items: The US military has spent over $47 billion on the war in Iran, exceeding previous estimates by more than 25%.
The rising costs of the war are impacting Republican candidates' support ahead of the upcoming elections, as well as President Trump's approval ratings.
The Pentagon's latest estimates include significant costs for replacing munitions and military equipment, with plans for potential escalation in combat operations after the midterm elections.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

WASHINGTON, USA – The US military has spent over $47 billion so far to prosecute the war in Iran, more than 25% higher than the Defense Department’s estimate in July, according to Pentagon data obtained by Reuters.
The Pentagon did not immediately respond to a request for comment on its estimate, which has not been shared publicly.

The disclosure about the rising cost of the Iran war comes as Republicans wrestle with the political fallout of the unpopular conflict ahead of the November 3 election that will determine control of Congress for the next two years.

The war’s impact on global energy costs has weighed on support for Republican candidates and hurt President Donald Trump’s approval ratings. Trump’s Republican Party holds a narrow majority in both chambers of Congress.
The Pentagon’s latest estimate was tied to the operational costs of carrying out the war, with a projected cost of more than $29 billion to replace expended munitions used in the conflict.
More than $6 billion would be needed to replace military equipment and so-called “platform losses,” which include the loss of aircraft including many drones lost during the war.
Trump launched the Iran war jointly with Israel in February, predicting ​that the conflict would last a short time.

Trump’s initial strategy in the Iran war focused on first using expensive, high-end precision missiles to bomb Iran’s defenses so it could later use less expensive munitions, including gravity bombs like the air-launched JDAMs, which are plentiful.
But an April ceasefire gave time for Iran to dig out underground storage facilities, bringing back online some Iranian defenses, as well as missiles and drones that had been inaccessible.

Trump has since imposed a naval blockade on Iran to starve it of oil export revenue and held out the possibility of restarting combat operations after the midterm elections. US officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, say the Pentagon has been planning to restart heavy fighting if ordered to do so.
The latest Pentagon estimate compares to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth‘s July estimate of $37.5 billion for the cost of the war.

While the figures include a host of operational costs, from flight operations to cyber support, the US military’s Iran war cost estimates did not clearly account for the massive expense expected to repair damage to US bases sustained by Iranian missile and drone attacks. Rappler.com

articles.title: ICC victims ask Chamber to admit witness testimony vs Rodrigo Duterte
articles.summary: The Common Legal Representatives of Victims (CLRV) has asked the International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III to grant the Prosecution"s request to admit the previously recorded testimonies…

blocks.text: Published October 28, 2026 9:50am

The Common Legal Representatives of Victims (CLRV) has asked the International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III to grant the Prosecution’s request to admit the previously recorded testimonies of three witnesses in the crimes against humanity case of former President Rodrigo Duterte.
In an eight-page document dated October 27, the CLRV said the testimonies do not appear to concern the acts of Duterte.
It said the testimonies appear relevant and corroborative to the accounts of other witnesses and relate primarily to the contextual elements of crimes against humanity.

“Furthermore, the CLRV supports the Request on the ground that the introduction of the prior recorded testimonies and related documents would be consistent with the victims’ rights to a fair and expeditious trial, and [REDACTED], [REDACTED],” it said.
According to the CLRV, the testimonies concern the alleged extrajudicial killings in Central Luzon and fall within the scope of Count 3.

“The prior recorded testimonies and related documents appear to have sufficient indicia of reliability, having been voluntarily recorded during the Prosecution’s investigation in the Philippines,” it said.
“Their introduction would also serve the interests of justice by contributing to the expeditious conduct of the proceedings and conserving the Court’s time and resources,” it added.
The document was signed by lawyers Gilbert Andres, Joel Butuyan, and Paolina Massida.
Duterte is facing charges of crimes against humanity in connection with the alleged extrajudicial killings in the war on drugs during his term as president and during his term as mayor of Davao City.
He was arrested in March 2025 at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Terminal 3 and is currently detained at the ICC Detention Center in Scheveningen in The Hague, the Netherlands.
Duterte's trial will start on November 30.
The ICC Trial Chamber III found Duterte fit to stand trial, stating that he “is able to effectively exercise his fair trial rights in the proceedings.” —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: SC: Employees cannot be forced to retire before age 65 without consent
articles.summary: In the case, the SC finds Colegio de San Juan de Letran in Laguna guilty of illegal dismissal

blocks.text: EMPLOYEES. A number of senior citizens participate in a pre-screening and orientation on March 18, 2026, at the Department of Manpower Development and Placement (DMDP) office in Cebu City for employment opportunities available to those aged 60 to 65 who are still willing and able to work.
Jacqueline Hernandez/Rappler
In the case, the SC finds Colegio de San Juan de Letran in Laguna guilty of illegal dismissal

items: The Supreme Court ruled that employers cannot force employees to retire early without their consent, affirming that the mandatory retirement age is 65.
In the case of Rodolfo Ondevilla, the Court found Colegio de San Juan de Letran guilty of illegal dismissal as there was no mutual agreement for his early retirement.
The ruling awarded Ondevilla full back wages, separation pay, and retirement benefits, emphasizing that his retirement was involuntary and treated as illegal dismissal.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – The Supreme Court (SC) has ruled that employers cannot force their employees to retire early without an agreement.

In a decision penned by Associate Justice Ramon Paul Hernando, and was made public on Tuesday, October 27, the SC 1st Division said employees cannot be made to retire from their position before the mandatory retirement age of 65 without their clear and voluntary consent.
Hernando, in the case, partly granted the petition of Rodolfo Ondevilla and found Colegio de San Juan de Letran (CSJL) in Laguna guilty of illegal dismissal.
Ondevilla asserted in his SC petition that he never agreed to retire before 65. The SC accepted his position.

Hernando explained that under the country’s Labor Code, the retirement age is set by an existing agreement or employment contract. If there’s no agreement or contract, then the mandatory retirement age of 65 will be applied, along with the minimum age for optional retirement of 60.

The ruling explained that optional retirement is based on a voluntary agreement between the employer and employee, and the latter must freely agree to it without pressure or coercion. But the SC said in the Ondevilla case that the early retirement happened despite the lack of a mutual agreement between the parties.

Based on the decision, the SC said CSJL never made any proposal for a retirement plan to the petitioner that he could accept or reject, adding that there was no indication that the school was willing to discuss Ondevilla’s retirement.

The High Court added Ondevilla’s objection to his supposed early retirement, along with his illegal dismissal complaint, showed that he had no intention of availing himself of optional retirement before reaching the age of 65.
“Because his retirement was involuntary, the SC treated it as an illegal dismissal. Ondevilla was therefore entitled to full back wages and separation pay instead of reinstatement,” said the ruling.

The SC also awarded him retirement benefits covering his employment from June 16, 2004, until August 29, 2024, when he reached the mandatory retirement age of 65. It directed the arbitration branch to compute the total amount due to him.
Ondevilla started working for CSJL as a comptroller in 2004, and later worked as assistant vice president for finance. He was renewed for work several times.

When the school had a management reorganization in 2018, he was reassigned as controller. Although he objected to this and said it was a demotion, he continued working with the same salary and employee benefits.
CJSL considered Ondevilla’s appointment expired on August 29, 2019, when he turned 60.
The petitioner then filed a complaint for illegal dismissal. He secured victories from the Labor Arbiter, and then from the National Labor Relations Commission.
The case reached the Court of Appeals (CA). It found that Ondevilla had been illegally dismissed, but ruled that a letter he sent to the school showed that he had agreed to retire on July 31, 2020.
When he filed the petition with the SC, Ondevilla challenged the CA’s findings and argued that he never agreed to retire early. – Rappler.com
